title: Sample efficiency of reinforcement learning
bottleneck: RL agents still need orders of magnitude more experience than humans to learn a task — millions of episodes for what a person grasps in minutes. RLHF inherits this: aligning a model to nuanced human preferences requires enormous volumes of human feedback, and the feedback itself is noisy and inconsistent. No method achieves human-like few-shot skill acquisition in complex environments. Preference data also suffers from labeler disagreement and sycophancy, compounding the sample-cost problem.
why_it_blocks: Every new capability costs a fortune in environment interactions or human labeler hours, making RL-based improvement slow and expensive to scale. Expensive feedback loops slow every capability iteration, not just alignment efforts.
current_state: Offline RL, model-based RL, and preference learning reduce but don't eliminate the gap. Human sample efficiency remains unmatched.
